ukmt-sk-2023-01.title: Match the heights
ukmt-sk-2023-01.body:
Let the small rectangle have sides $a<b$. The flag's height equals the long side $b$ of an upright rectangle on the left, and also equals three short sides stacked in the middle, $3a$. So $b=3a$, $\lambda=\frac13$ and $360\lambda=120$.

**Answer: 120**

ukmt-sk-2023-02.title: Factor out powers of 3
ukmt-sk-2023-02.body:
$7!+8!+9!=7!(1+8+72)=7!\times81=2^4\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7\times3^4=2^4\cdot3^6\cdot5\cdot7$. The smallest $n$ takes the largest $m=6$, giving $n=2^4\cdot5\cdot7=560$.

**Answer: 560**

ukmt-sk-2023-03.title: Multiples of 512
ukmt-sk-2023-03.body:
The multiples of $2^9=512$ in the range are $512k$ with $2\cdot512\le512k\le512\cdot512$, i.e. $k=2,\dots,512$: that is $511$ integers.

**Answer: 511**

ukmt-sk-2023-04.title: Check each month
ukmt-sk-2023-04.body:
January ($7>1$), February ($8>2$), March ($5>3$) and April ($5>4$) work; May ($3$), June ($4$) and later months fail since the label exceeds the letter count. 2024 is a leap year: $31+29+31+30=121$ days.

**Answer: 121**

ukmt-sk-2023-05.title: Bound n
ukmt-sk-2023-05.body:
The second largest factor of $n$ is at most $n/2$, so $n-6\le n/2$ and $n\le12$. Testing $n=7,\dots,12$: $7$ (second largest factor $1=7-6$), $9$ ($3=9-6$) and $12$ ($6=12-6$) work; $8,10,11$ do not. So $C=7+9+12=28$ and $11C=308$.

**Answer: 308**

ukmt-sk-2023-06.title: Case on card 101
ukmt-sk-2023-06.body:
If 101 is true, then 102 and 104 are false, so 105 is true and 103 is false. That makes exactly two true cards (101, 105), so 102 would be true: contradiction. So 101 is false. Then 102 is true and 104 is true; 105 is false and 103 is false. Exactly two are true, consistent. The sum is $102+104=206$.

**Answer: 206**

ukmt-sk-2023-07.title: Face areas
ukmt-sk-2023-07.body:
Let the dimensions be $x,y,z$. The water forms boxes of volume $120$ with depths $2,3,5$ over the three different faces: $5xy=3xz=2yz=120$ (with the face of area $xy$ being the one for depth $5$, etc.). Multiply: $30x^2y^2z^2=120^3$, so $(xyz)^2=\frac{120^3}{30}=4\cdot120^2$ and $xyz=240$.

**Answer: 240**

ukmt-sk-2023-09.title: Try cubes
ukmt-sk-2023-09.body:
$1+13=14$, $8+13=21$, $27+13=40$, $64+13=77$, $125+13=138$ are not prime (all are composite, and for odd cubes the sum is even). $216+13=229$ is prime.

**Answer: 229**

ukmt-sk-2023-10.title: Find the primes
ukmt-sk-2023-10.body:
The smallest two-digit primes are $11,13,17,19$. Pair sums: $24=11+13$ and $28=11+17$ (no other pair gives $24$ or $28$). These are a row and a column sharing $11$, so $13$ and $17$ are adjacent to $11$ and $19$ is opposite. The other sums are $13+19=32$ and $17+19=36$. So $5\cdot32+7\cdot36=160+252=412$.

**Answer: 412**

ukmt-sk-2023-11.title: Build up
ukmt-sk-2023-11.body:
Total: $25+16+9+4+1=55$ p. The coins of values $1,2$ pay every amount from $0$ to $5$ ($1,2,1+2,2+2,1+2+2$). Adding up to three $3$ p coins extends this to every amount from $0$ to $5+9=14$ (each new coin value is at most one more than the current maximum, so no gaps). Adding up to four $4$ p coins gives $0$ to $30$; adding up to five $5$ p coins gives $0$ to $55$. So every amount up to $55$ p can be paid, and $56$ p exceeds his total.

**Answer: 56**

ukmt-sk-2023-12.title: Compositions of 6
ukmt-sk-2023-12.body:
Each such integer corresponds to an ordered way of writing $6$ as a sum of positive integers (each at most $9$, automatically): a composition of $6$. There are $2^{6-1}=32$ compositions.

**Answer: 32**

ukmt-sk-2023-13.title: Pythagoras
ukmt-sk-2023-13.body:
Take side $1$, so $CE=\lambda$ and $BE=\sqrt{1+\lambda^2}$. The perimeter condition: $1+\lambda+\sqrt{1+\lambda^2}=3$, so $\sqrt{1+\lambda^2}=2-\lambda$ and $1+\lambda^2=4-4\lambda+\lambda^2$, giving $\lambda=\frac34$. Then $960\lambda=720$.

**Answer: 720**

ukmt-sk-2023-14.title: Count progressions
ukmt-sk-2023-14.body:
There are $\binom{10}3=120$ equally likely choices. One of three numbers is the mean of the other two exactly when they form an arithmetic progression. The numbers correspond to $1,\dots,10$ (via $k\mapsto2k-1$) and the number of $3$-term progressions with common difference $d$ is $10-2d$ for $d=1,\dots,4$: $8+6+4+2=20$. So $p=\frac{20}{120}=\frac16$ and $\frac{120}p=720$.

**Answer: 720**

ukmt-sk-2023-15.title: Complement
ukmt-sk-2023-15.body:
The game is lost when both marbles are blue: $\frac B{21}\cdot\frac{B-1}{20}=\frac12$, so $B^2-B-210=0$, $(B-15)(B+14)=0$ and $B=15$, $R=6$. Then $B^2+R^2=225+36=261$.

**Answer: 261**

ukmt-sk-2023-16.title: Equally likely displays
ukmt-sk-2023-16.body:
Each of the $2^7=128$ on/off patterns is equally likely, and exactly $10$ of them show the digits $0$ to $9$. The probability is $\frac{10}{128}=\frac5{64}$, so $9\cdot5+2\cdot64=173$.

**Answer: 173**

ukmt-sk-2023-17.title: Squeeze
ukmt-sk-2023-17.body:
The expression is greater than $\sqrt{64}=8$, so $A\ge8$. If the innermost $72$ were replaced by $81$, then each layer would give $\sqrt{72+9}=9$ in turn, so the whole expression would be $9$. Since we replaced a smaller number by a larger one, the original is less than $9$. So $A=8$ and $50A=400$.

**Answer: 400**

ukmt-sk-2023-18.title: Coprime to 20
ukmt-sk-2023-18.body:
HCF$(20,YY)=1$ exactly when $YY$ is coprime to $20=2^2\cdot5$, i.e. odd and not a multiple of $5$: last digit $1,3,7,9$. For $2026$ to $2029$: $2027,2029$ ($2$ years). Each of the decades $2030$s to $2090$s (seven) has $4$ such years. Total $2+7\cdot4=30$.

**Answer: 30**

ukmt-sk-2023-19.title: Factorise
ukmt-sk-2023-19.body:
$290224=2^4\cdot11\cdot17\cdot97$. The product of any two of $11,17,97$ is at least $187$, and $16\cdot11=176$ is three-digit, so the two-digit factors are $11,17,97$ and their multiples by powers of $2$ that stay two-digit, plus $16$: $11,22,44,88;\ 17,34,68;\ 97;\ 16$. Their sum is $165+119+97+16=397$.

**Answer: 397**

ukmt-sk-2023-20.title: Fill the grid
ukmt-sk-2023-20.body:
The two-digit factors of $105$ are $15,21,35$, so 1 ACROSS is $11$, $17$ or $31$. A three-digit number that is $400$ less than a cube with non-zero digits is $112$, $329$ or $931$; 2 DOWN starts with the second digit of 1 ACROSS, which is $1$ or $7$, so 2 DOWN is $112$ and 1 ACROSS is $11$ or $31$ (not $17$).

If 1 ACROSS is $11$: 1 DOWN is $14$ ($16-2$), and 3 ACROSS starts with $4$ and has middle digit $1$: $415$ ($414+1$). Then 4 DOWN is $5x$ (its top digit is the last digit of $415$), i.e. between $51$ and $59$, and must be six less than the sum of two other answers; but $11+14-6=19$, and sums involving 5 ACROSS (between $21$ and $29$) give at most $29+14-6=37$, while sums involving $415$ or $112$ are far too large. Impossible.

So 1 ACROSS is $31$, 1 DOWN is $34$ ($36-2$) and 3 ACROSS is $415$. 4 DOWN is $5x$ and equals $31+34-6=59$, so $x=9$. 5 ACROSS is $2\,9=29$, and its square is $841$.

**Answer: 841**
